pr.title: Don't inline tainted MIR bodies
pr.description:
Don't inline MIR bodies that are tainted, since they're not necessarily well-formed.

Fixes #128601 (I didn't add a new test, just copied one from the crashes, since they're the same root cause).
Fixes #122909.
pr.author: compiler-errors

analysis.originalLogic: In `Inliner::check_mir_body`, the inliner evaluated a callee MIR body's eligibility for MIR inlining—including the inline threshold/cost logic—without first checking `callee_body.tainted_by_errors`. A body produced during error recovery could therefore be treated like an ordinary, well-formed inlining candidate and passed on to `try_inlining`.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historically incorrect transformation was to inline/copy a callee MIR body whose `tainted_by_errors` field was `Some(_)`. Such a body is not necessarily well-formed, so later inlining logic may make invalid assumptions about its shape, such as closure arguments being passed as a tuple or mentioned items being initialized. The correct transformation rejects the candidate before threshold/cost evaluation with `return Err("Body is tainted")`.
analysis.inputDomain: Rust programs that already produce type/ABI/well-formedness errors but continue through error recovery into MIR optimization, where an error-tainted callee body is considered for MIR inlining. The regression input uses an unused type parameter, an invalid `extern "rust-call" fn try_get(&self) -> Option<Arc<T>>` signature/body, and expected mismatched-types diagnostics. It is compiled with `-Zvalidate-mir -Zinline-mir=yes`; the linked ICE reports also used `-Zpolymorphize=on`. Valid crates with no error-tainted MIR body are outside this triggering domain.
analysis.summary: Bug fix for MIR inlining: `Inliner::check_mir_body` now rejects callee bodies marked `tainted_by_errors` before performing the inline threshold/cost checks. Tainted error-recovery MIR is not necessarily well-formed, and inlining it could lead to ICEs such as the closure-argument tuple assertion or missing `mentioned_items`. The regression was moved from `tests/crashes/122909.rs` to a UI test under `tests/ui/polymorphization/inline-tainted-body.rs` with expected diagnostics and no ICE. This knowledge comes from the patch and linked issue text; no compiler was built or run.
analysis.trigger: While compiling an already-invalid crate with MIR inlining enabled, the inliner considers a callee whose MIR body has `tainted_by_errors = Some(_)`; before the fix, `check_mir_body` does not reject it early.
preconditions: The crate continues to MIR optimization after emitting errors, so an error-tainted MIR body exists.
The inliner considers that tainted body as a callee candidate.
The body is not guaranteed to be well-formed, so shape-sensitive inlining logic may be reached.
pitfalls: Do not treat error-tainted MIR as ordinary well-formed MIR merely because the inliner has a body available.
The taint check belongs before threshold/cost and other body-shape assumptions; a later check can already have relied on malformed MIR.
`tainted_by_errors` is an `Option`; the historical fix checks for `Some(_)`, not a boolean flag.
The test remains a compile-fail test: success means emitting the expected normal diagnostics without an ICE, not compiling successfully.

The linked issues used `-Zpolymorphize=on`, but the added UI regression uses only `-Zvalidate-mir -Zinline-mir=yes`, so the taint rejection is an inliner invariant rather than a polymorphization-only fix.
Do not infer that every invalid program will hit this path; the specific condition is a tainted callee body being considered for inlining.
analysis.testStrategy: Add a UI compile-fail regression under `tests/ui/polymorphization/` with `//@ compile-flags: -Zvalidate-mir -Zinline-mir=yes`. Use the reduced invalid program that creates a tainted callee body, and expect only the ordinary diagnostics (unused type parameter E0392, invalid `rust-call` ABI, E0308 mismatched types) with no compiler panic. The historical test promotion deleted the old `tests/crashes/122909.rs` containing `//@ known-bug: #122909` and added `inline-tainted-body.rs` plus an explicit `.stderr`. For a focused differential check, compile the same invalid input with inlining enabled versus disabled and verify that the extra inlining-related ICE appears only in the enabled configuration, while normal diagnostics remain.
evidence: Don't inline MIR bodies that are tainted, since they're not necessarily well-formed.
Fixes #128601 (I didn't add a new test, just copied one from the crashes, since they're the same root cause).
